title: Career Roadmap: Financial Analyst
summary: Analyse financial statements, business performance, budgets and market trends to help organizations make informed decisions about investments, costs, profitability and financial planning.

facts.Current degree: Liberal Arts / Liberal Studies (BA / B.Sc Liberal Arts & Sciences)

about.label: Education Pathway
about.text: Liberal Arts / Liberal Studies – Economics & Finance (Liberal)

blocks.text: Analyse financial statements, business performance, budgets and market trends to help organizations make informed decisions about investments, costs, profitability and financial planning.

rows.text: Any stream, subject to programme eligibility; Mathematics, Accountancy and Economics are useful
Liberal Arts degree with a concentration in Economics & Finance
Corporate finance, investment analysis, financial planning, equity research or risk analysis
MBA Finance, M.Sc. Finance, Economics or Financial Analytics, where beneficial

blocks.label: Alternative pathways
blocks.text: B.Com., BBA Finance, B.A. Economics, B.Sc. Economics or another relevant degree with strong quantitative and accounting coursework.

blocks.label: Financial Statements
blocks.text: Income statements, balance sheets, cash-flow statements and financial ratios.

blocks.label: Financial Modelling
blocks.text: Forecasting, budgeting, valuation and scenario analysis.

blocks.label: Tools
blocks.text: Excel, PowerPoint and financial databases; SQL and Power BI are useful additional skills.

blocks.label: Quantitative Analysis
blocks.text: Statistics, time value of money, risk-return analysis and economic indicators.

blocks.label: Business Understanding
blocks.text: Revenue drivers, cost structures, profitability and industry trends.

blocks.label: Communication
blocks.text: Financial reports, presentations and evidence-based recommendations.
Build three or four practical finance projects:

blocks.label: Financial Statement Analysis
blocks.text: Evaluate a listed company's financial health using annual reports.

blocks.label: Financial Model
blocks.text: Build a three-statement forecast for a sample business.

blocks.label: Company Valuation
blocks.text: Prepare a basic discounted cash flow (DCF) valuation with documented assumptions.

blocks.label: Budget & Variance Analysis
blocks.text: Compare actual and budgeted performance and explain the differences.

blocks.label: Industry Comparison
blocks.text: Compare financial ratios across two or three companies in the same sector.
Use publicly available financial information and clearly distinguish assumptions from reported figures.
Target placements at:

items.text: Corporate treasury and business planning teams.

blocks.text: Search for Financial Analyst Intern, FP&A Intern, Equity Research Intern, Finance Intern and Investment Analyst Intern roles.
Prioritize:

items.text: Accounting fundamentals and financial statement analysis.
Power BI or other reporting tools.
SQL and Python for financial analytics.
CFA or FRM preparation if aligned with investment or risk career goals.

blocks.text: Check the eligibility and professional requirements for any certification before enrolling. Certifications complement but do not replace practical financial analysis.
Finance Intern / Financial Planning Intern
Junior Financial Analyst
Financial Analyst / FP&A Analyst
Senior Analyst → Finance Manager / Finance Lead
Investment research, corporate finance, risk and FP&A are distinct specializations with different technical requirements.

items.text: Risk Analyst, with relevant additional training

rows.text: Learn accounting fundamentals, financial statements, Excel and financial ratios.
Build a financial model and analyse a listed company's annual report.
Complete a valuation or budgeting project, prepare a finance-focused résumé and apply for internships.

blocks.label: Target-ready profile
blocks.text: Strong Excel skills, financial statement analysis, basic valuation and forecasting, quantitative reasoning and a portfolio demonstrating practical financial decision-making.
